subject: CPC
question: As per the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, _____ means the presiding officer of a civil Court.
explanation: A judge presides over a civil court.
cue: A judge presides over a civil court.

subject: CPC
question: Under the C.P.C, "_____" means the statement given by the Judge of the grounds of a decree or order.

cue: Judgment gives reasons; decree formally declares the adjudicated rights.

subject: CPC
question: As per the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, _____ means the formal expression of an adjudication which, so far as regards the Court expressing it, conclusively determines the rights of the parties which regard to all or any of the matters in controversy in the suit.
explanation: A decree conclusively determines rights in the suit.

subject: CPC
question: A decree is an operative part of _____ in civil law.
explanation: The judgment explains the reasons; the decree states the operative result.

subject: CPC
question: Decree-holder is _____.
options: Any person in whose favour a decree has been passed
An order capable of execution has been made

cue: The definition covers a person favoured by a decree or an executable order; option B is grammatically abbreviated.

subject: CPC
question: Consent decree is _____.
explanation: No appeal lies from a decree passed with the parties' consent.
cue: No appeal lies from a decree passed with the parties' consent.

subject: CPC
question: As per Section 2(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908, "Codes" includes _____.
explanation: Code includes rules. The source prints Codes in the plural.
cue: Code includes rules

subject: CPC
question: As per Section 2(8) of The Code of Civil Procedure 1908, "Judge" means presiding officer of _____.
explanation: This CPC definition concerns a civil court.
cue: This CPC definition concerns a civil court.

subject: CPC
question: As per Section 2(9) of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908, "Judgment" means the statement given by the _____ of the grounds of a decree or order.
explanation: A judge states the grounds of the decree or order.
cue: A judge states the grounds of the decree or order.

subject: CPC
question: As per Section 2(10) of The Code of Civil Procedure 1908, _____ means any person against whom a decree has been passed or an order capable of execution has been made.
explanation: Debtor means the person against whom the executable decision operates.
cue: Debtor means the person against whom the executable decision operates.

subject: CPC
question: As per section 2(13) of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908, "Movable Property" includes _____.
explanation: The definition expressly includes growing crops.
cue: The definition expressly includes growing crops.

subject: CPC
question: As per Section 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908, For the purposes of this Code, the District Court is subordinate to the High Court, and every Civil Court of a grade inferior to that of a District Court and every Court of Small Causes is subordinate to the High Court and _____ Court.
explanation: The inferior civil courts and small-causes courts are subordinate to the District Court as well.
cue: The inferior civil courts and small-causes courts are subordinate to the District Court as well.

subject: CPC
question: The rules for transferring execution of certain decrees, in any local area, to the collector shall be declared by notification in the official gazette of _____ Government.
explanation: Section 68 assigns the declaration to the Provincial Government.
cue: Section 68 assigns the declaration to the Provincial Government.

subject: CPC
question: Under the CPC, a decree passed with the consent of the parties is known as _____.
explanation: A compromise decree records the parties' lawful agreement.
cue: A compromise decree records the parties' lawful agreement.

subject: CPC
question: As per section 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, the Courts shall (subject to the provisions contained in the CPC) have jurisdiction to try all suits of a _____ excepting suits of which their cognizance is either expressly or impliedly barred.
explanation: Civil courts try suits of a civil nature unless jurisdiction is barred.
cue: Civil courts try suits of a civil nature unless jurisdiction is barred.

subject: CPC
question: Civil matters are decided on the basis of _____.
explanation: Balance of probabilities is the ordinary civil standard; beyond reasonable doubt belongs to criminal proof.
cue: Balance of probabilities is the ordinary civil standard; beyond reasonable doubt belongs to criminal proof.

subject: CPC
question: Principle of Res Sub-judice is contained in _____ of CPC.
explanation: Sub judice concerns a previously instituted suit still pending.
cue: Sub judice concerns a previously instituted suit still pending.

subject: CPC
question: Which of the following does not deals with final determination of contested questions and have the binding effect in future litigation?
explanation: Res sub judice concerns pending litigation, not a finally decided matter.
cue: Res sub judice concerns pending litigation, not a finally decided matter.

subject: CPC
question: Section _____ of the C.P.C prevents courts of concurrent jurisdiction from simultaneously entertaining and adjudicating upon two parallel litigations in respect of the same matter in issue.
explanation: Section 10 stays the trial subject to its conditions; it does not itself prohibit institution of the later suit.
cue: Section 10 stays the trial subject to its conditions; it does not itself prohibit institution of the later suit.

subject: CPC
question: Under the CPC, no court shall proceed the trial of any suit on same cause of action which is pending before _____.
explanation: The intended answer is D, but the stem is overbroad: the previously instituted suit, parties, substantial issues and competent jurisdiction must satisfy section 10.
cue: The intended answer is D, but the stem is overbroad: the previously instituted suit, parties, substantial issues and competent jurisdiction must satisfy section 10.

subject: CPC
question: As per Sections 10 and 11 of The Code of Civil Procedure 1908, one of the differences between "res-judicata" and "res sub-judice" is that in one case the suit _____.
options: Has been decided while pending in other case
Is in appeal while pending in other case
Is in execution while pending in other case
Is in execution while stay in other case
explanation: Judicata: decided. Sub judice: pending.
cue: Judicata: decided

subject: CPC
question: Constructive res-judicata is contained in _____.
explanation: A matter which might and ought to have been raised is treated as directly and substantially in issue.
cue: A matter which might and ought to have been raised is treated as directly and substantially in issue.

subject: CPC
question: A decision or finding given by a court or a tribunal without jurisdiction _____.
options: Can operate as res-judicata under all circumstances
Can operate as res-judicata under certain circumstances only
May operates as res-judicata or may not operates as res-judicata
explanation: A competent court is required for the statutory rule of res judicata.
cue: A competent court is required for the statutory rule of res judicata.

subject: CPC
question: In a suit, where the doctrine of res-judicata applies, the suit is liable to be _____.
options: May be stayed & may be dismissed
explanation: Res judicata bars retrial of the decided issue; a mere stay describes section 10 instead.
cue: Res judicata bars retrial of the decided issue; a mere stay describes section 10 instead.

subject: CPC
question: Principle of res-judicata applies _____.
options: To suits as well as execution proceedings
explanation: The book applies the principle to suits and execution proceedings. This extension requires case-law treatment beyond the bare wording of section 11.
cue: The book applies the principle to suits and execution proceedings

subject: CPC
question: Where a plaintiff is precluded by rules from institute further suit in respect of any particular cause of action, he _____ to institute a suit in respect of such cause of action in any Court to which this Code applies.
explanation: The statutory phrase is shall not be entitled.
cue: The statutory phrase is shall not be entitled.

subject: CPC
question: As per Civil Procedure Code 1908, section 12(2), where a person challenges the validity of a judgment, decree or order, he shall seek his remedy by making an application to the court which passed the final judgment
explanation: Fraud, misrepresentation and want of jurisdiction are all grounds addressed by section 12(2).
cue: Fraud, misrepresentation and want of jurisdiction are all grounds addressed by section 12(2).

subject: CPC
question: Bar to further suit is dealt under which of the following in the Code of Civil Procedure.
explanation: No option gives section 12, whose heading is Bar to further suit. The printed key D is unsafe; excluded from scored practice.
cue: No option gives section 12, whose heading is Bar to further suit

subject: CPC
question: As per section 15 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, every suit shall be instituted in the Court of the lowest grade competent to try it, EXCEPT:
options: For the recovery of immovable property-with or without rent or profits
For the partition of immovable property
explanation: An appeal is not institution of an original suit under section 15.
cue: An appeal is not institution of an original suit under section 15.

subject: CPC
question: As per explanation to Section 16 (where suits to be instituted) of the code of Civil Procedure 1908, "Property" means property situated _____.
explanation: The explanation means property situated in Pakistan.
cue: The explanation means property situated in Pakistan.

subject: CPC
question: A suit for compensation for wrong done to the person or to moveable property, where the wrong was done within the local jurisdiction of one court and the defendant resides within the local limits of another court.
options: Can be instituted in the Court within whose local jurisdiction the wrong has been committed
Can be instituted in the court within whose local jurisdiction the defendant resides
Either A or B at the option of the plaintiff
explanation: The plaintiff may choose either court specified by section 19.
cue: The plaintiff may choose either court specified by section 19.

subject: CPC
question: Suits for the recovery of movable property actually under distant or attachment shall be instituted in the Court within the local limit of whose jurisdiction the _____.
explanation: The statute says distraint or attachment; the book misprints distant. The property's location supplies the venue.
cue: The statute says distraint or attachment; the book misprints distant

subject: CPC
question: Suit in respect of immovable property, where the entire relief sought can be obtained through the personal obedience of the defendant, can be instituted in a court within whose local jurisdiction.
options: The defendant voluntarily resides or carries on business
The defendant voluntarily resides or personally works for gain
explanation: The proviso permits these alternatives where its conditions, including personal obedience, are satisfied.
cue: The proviso permits these alternatives where its conditions, including personal obedience, are satisfied.

subject: CPC
question: As per Section 16(b) of The Code of Civil Procedure 1908, subject to the pecuniary or other limitations prescribed by law, for the partition of immovable property, suit shall be instituted where _____.
options: The cause of action is wholly or partly arisen
explanation: Partition normally follows the location of the immovable property.
cue: Partition normally follows the location of the immovable property.

subject: CPC
question: As per Section 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908, where a suit to obtain relief respecting, or compensation for wrong to immovable property situate within the jurisdiction of _____ Courts, the suit may be instituted in any Court within the local limits of whose jurisdiction any portion of the property is situate.
explanation: Different courts may have territorial portions; the chosen court must be competent regarding the value of the entire claim.
cue: Different courts may have territorial portions; the chosen court must be competent regarding the value of the entire claim.

subject: CPC
question: The word 'resides' used in section 19 of the Code of Civil Procedure means _____.
explanation: The book chooses natural persons. Corporate venue is dealt with through business and statutory explanations; this interpretive answer has not been independently case-law verified.
cue: The book chooses natural persons

subject: CPC
question: As per section 19 of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908, Where a suit is for compensation for wrong done to the person or to movable property, if the wrong was done within the local limits of the Jurisdiction of one Court and the defendant resides, or carries on business, or personally works for gain, within the local limits of the Jurisdiction of another Court, the suit may be instituted at the option of the _____ either of the said Courts.
explanation: The choice belongs to the plaintiff.
cue: The choice belongs to the plaintiff.

subject: CPC
question: According to illustration (b) of Section 19 of The Code of Civil Procedure 1908, A, residing in Karachi, published in Quetta statements defamatory of B. B may Sue A _____.
options: Either in Quetta or in Karachi
explanation: One venue is the wrong's location and the other is the defendant's residence.
cue: One venue is the wrong's location and the other is the defendant's residence.

subject: CPC
question: As per section 20 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, suits are to be instituted where _____ reside or cause of action arises.
explanation: Section 20 uses the defendant's residence or business/work, or the cause of action, subject to its conditions.
cue: Section 20 uses the defendant's residence or business/work, or the cause of action, subject to its conditions.

subject: CPC
question: As per Section 20(c) of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908, subject to the limitations mentioned in the CPC, every suit _____ instituted in a Court within the local limits of whose jurisdiction, the cause of action, wholly or in part arises.
explanation: The complete phrase is shall be instituted. The printed key C leaves the sentence incomplete.
cue: The complete phrase is shall be instituted

subject: CPC
question: As per Order 41(15) of The Code of Civil Procedure 1908, the notice to the respondent shall declare that if he does not appear in the Appellate Court on the day so fixed the appeal will be _____.
explanation: The warning is that the appeal will be heard ex parte.
cue: The warning is that the appeal will be heard ex parte.

subject: CPC
question: As per Section 47(1) of The Code of Civil Procedure 1908, all questions arising _____ in which the decree was passed, or their representatives, and relating to the execution, discharge, or satisfaction of the decree, shall be determined by the Court executing the decree and not by a separate suit.
options: Between the legal heirs of a party
Between the parties to the suit
From the claimant to the suit
From the respondent to the suit
explanation: Execution questions between the parties or their representatives go to the executing court.
cue: Execution questions between the parties or their representatives go to the executing court.

subject: CPC
question: As per Section 47(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908, the Court may, subject to _____ objection as to limitation or jurisdiction, treat a proceeding under this section as a suit or a suit as a proceeding and may, if necessary, order payment of any additional court-fees.
explanation: The provision preserves any objection concerning limitation or jurisdiction.
cue: The provision preserves any objection concerning limitation or jurisdiction.

subject: CPC
question: As per Civil Procedure Code 1908, Section 75, Subject to such Conditions and limitations as may be prescribed, the Court may issue a commission EXCEPT _____.
explanation: A local investigation is listed; a criminal investigation is not.
cue: A local investigation is listed; a criminal investigation is not.

subject: CPC
question: As per section 75 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, subject to such conditions and limitations as may be prescribed by the Court, the Court may issue a commission of all the following EXCEPT:
explanation: Issuing the decree is a judicial function, not a purpose listed for a commission.
cue: Issuing the decree is a judicial function, not a purpose listed for a commission.

subject: CPC
question: As per Section 75(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908, subject to such conditions and limitations as may be prescribed the Court may issue a/an _____ to make a partition.
explanation: Partition is one of the statutory purposes for a commission.
cue: Partition is one of the statutory purposes for a commission.

subject: CPC
question: As per section 96(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, an appeal shall lie from every _____ passed by any court of original jurisdiction.
explanation: Subject to statutory exceptions, section 96 concerns appeals from original decrees.
cue: Subject to statutory exceptions, section 96 concerns appeals from original decrees.

subject: CPC
question: As per section 96(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908, may lie from an original decree passed ex-parte.
explanation: An ex parte decree can be appealed; Order IX rule 13 is a distinct remedy.
cue: An ex parte decree can be appealed; Order IX rule 13 is a distinct remedy.

subject: CPC
question: As per section 96(3) of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908, no appeal shall lie from a decree passed by the Court _____.
options: Under the supervision of the Judge of High Court
Under the supervision of the Judge of Supreme Court
explanation: Consent decrees are excluded by subsection (3).
cue: Consent decrees are excluded by subsection (3).

subject: CPC
question: Section 104 of the CPC deals with _____.
options: Appeal from final decree where no appeal from preliminary decree
explanation: Section 104 identifies appealable orders.
cue: Section 104 identifies appealable orders.

subject: CPC
question: As per section 104 of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908, an appeal shall lie from the following orders EXCEPT:
options: Any order passed in appeal under section 104
Any order made under rules from which an appeal is expressly allowed
explanation: Subsection (2) expressly bars another appeal from an order passed in appeal under this section. The printed key D is wrong.
cue: Subsection (2) expressly bars another appeal from an order passed in appeal under this section

subject: CPC
question: As per Section 104(1)(h) of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908, an appeal shall lie from an order under any of the provisions of this Code imposing _____ or directing the arrest or detention in the civil prison of any person except where such arrest or detention is in execution of a decree.
explanation: The provision expressly says a fine.
cue: The provision expressly says a fine.

subject: CPC
question: As per Section 104(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908, _____ appeal shall lie from any order passed in appeal under this section.
explanation: No further appeal lies under this subsection.
cue: No further appeal lies under this subsection.

subject: CPC
question: Time limitation for filing revision petition before High Court is provided under section 115 of the CPC is _____ days.
explanation: The cited Pakistan Code text specifies ninety days. Provincial amendments and the applicable jurisdiction must be checked for real litigation.
cue: The cited Pakistan Code text specifies ninety days

subject: CPC
question: As per section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, The High Court may call for the record of any case which has been decided by any Court subordinate to such High Court and in which no appeal lies thereto, and if such subordinate Court appears as following EXCEPT:
options: To have exercised a jurisdiction not vested in it by law
To have failed to exercise a jurisdiction so vested
To have failed to exercise a jurisdiction not vested
To have acted in the exercise of its jurisdiction illegally or with material irregularity
explanation: Failure to exercise jurisdiction that was never vested is not a revision ground. The printed key D is wrong.
cue: Failure to exercise jurisdiction that was never vested is not a revision ground

subject: CPC
question: As per Section 115(1)(b) of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908, the High Court may call for the _____ of any case which has been decided by any Court subordinate to such High Court and in which no appeal lies thereto, and if such subordinate Court appears to have failed to exercise a jurisdiction so vested.
explanation: The High Court calls for the record.
cue: The High Court calls for the record.

subject: CPC
question: Under CPC, no proceedings in revision _____ be entertained by the High Court against an order made under section 115(2) by the District Court.
explanation: The prohibition is expressed as no proceedings shall be entertained.
cue: The prohibition is expressed as no proceedings shall be entertained.

subject: CPC
question: As per Section 115(2) of the code of civil procedure, 1908, the district court may exercise the powers conferred on the High Court by sub section (1) in respect of any case decided by a court subordinate to the such district court in which _____ appeal lies, and the amount or value of the subject-matter whereof does not exceed the limits of the appellate jurisdiction of the district court.
explanation: The subsection requires a case in which no appeal lies and the stated value limitation.
cue: The subsection requires a case in which no appeal lies and the stated value limitation.

subject: CPC
question: As per section 115(4) of the C.P.C, no proceeding in revision shall be entertained by the _____ against an order made under subsections (2) by the District Court.
explanation: The express prohibition names the High Court.
cue: The express prohibition names the High Court.

subject: CPC
question: As per section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, nothing in this code shall be deemed to limit or otherwise affect the _____ of the court to make such orders as may be necessary for the ends of justice or to prevent abuse of the process of the court.
explanation: Section 151 saves inherent powers to secure justice and prevent abuse.
cue: Section 151 saves inherent powers to secure justice and prevent abuse.

subject: CPC
question: As per Order I Rule 1 of CPC 1908, all persons may be joined in one suit as _____ in whom any right to relief in respect of or arising out of the same act or transaction or series of acts or transactions is alleged to exist, whether jointly, severly or in the alternative, where if such persons brought separate suits, any common question of law or fact would arise.
explanation: Rule 1 concerns joinder of plaintiffs; common transactions and common questions are required.
cue: Rule 1 concerns joinder of plaintiffs; common transactions and common questions are required.

subject: CPC
question: According to Order 1, Rule 4(b) of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908, Judgment may be given without any amendment against such one or more of the defendants as may be found to be liable, according to their respective _____.
explanation: Judgment follows the defendants' respective liabilities.
cue: Judgment follows the defendants' respective liabilities.

subject: CPC
question: As per Order I Rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908, it shall not be necessary that every defendant shall be interested as to _____ claimed in any suit against him.
explanation: Each defendant need not be interested in all relief claimed.
cue: Each defendant need not be interested in all relief claimed.

subject: CPC
question: As per Order I, rule 10(3) of the C.P.C, "No person shall be added as a plaintiff suing without a next friend or as the next friend of a plaintiff under any disability without _____?"
explanation: The person's consent is required.
cue: The person's consent is required.

subject: CPC
question: As per Order VI, Rule 1 of The Code of Civil Procedure 1908, _____ shall mean plaint or written statement.
explanation: Pleading is the umbrella term for plaint and written statement.
cue: Pleading is the umbrella term for plaint and written statement.

subject: CPC
question: According to Order VI Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908, every pleading shall contain, and contain only, a statement in a concise form of the _____ on which the party pleading relies for his claim or defense, as the case may be.
explanation: Plead material facts, not the evidence proving them.
cue: Plead material facts, not the evidence proving them.

subject: CPC
question: As per Order VI Rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908, the form in _____ when applicable, and where they are not applicable forms of the like character, as nearly as may be, shall be used for all pleadings.
explanation: Pleading forms are in Appendix A.
cue: Pleading forms are in Appendix A.

subject: CPC
question: According to the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 Order VI Rule 7, no pleading shall, except by way of amendment, raise any new ground of claim or contain any _____ of fact inconsistent with the previous pleadings of the party pleading the same.
explanation: A new inconsistent allegation requires amendment.
cue: A new inconsistent allegation requires amendment.

subject: CPC
question: When consider action is done at the time of contract is called _____.
explanation: The book means consideration performed at the time of contract: present consideration. This question is not a CPC provision.
cue: The book means consideration performed at the time of contract: present consideration

subject: CPC
question: _____ is the paramount consideration for the court while deciding custody of minor.
explanation: The child's welfare is central. This is family/guardianship law rather than a CPC provision; the cited Act still needs independent source checking.
cue: The child's welfare is central

subject: CPC
question: As per Order VI Rule 16 of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908, the Court may at any stage of the proceedings order to be struck out or amend any matter in any pleading which may be unnecessary or scandalous or which may tend to prejudice, embarrass, or delay the _____ of the suit.
explanation: The provision protects the fair trial of the suit.
cue: The provision protects the fair trial of the suit.

subject: CPC
question: As per Order VII, Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908, where the plaintiff seeks the recovery of money, the plaint shall state the precise _____.
explanation: State the precise amount claimed; the rule also provides for certain approximate statements.
cue: State the precise amount claimed; the rule also provides for certain approximate statements.

subject: CPC
question: Which of the following deals with where the subject-matter of the suit is immovable property in the Code of Civil Procedure?
explanation: Rule 3 requires sufficient identification of immovable property.
cue: Rule 3 requires sufficient identification of immovable property.

subject: CPC
question: As per Order VII Rule 10(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908, the plaint shall at any stage of the suit be returned to be presented to the Court in which the suit should have been _____.
explanation: Return sends the plaint to the proper court for institution.
cue: Return sends the plaint to the proper court for institution.

subject: CPC
question: Rejection of plaint under order 7 Rule 11 of the CPC is a/an _____.
explanation: Rejection of a plaint is expressly included in the definition of decree.
cue: Rejection of a plaint is expressly included in the definition of decree.

subject: CPC
question: A plaint can be rejected only on any of the _____ grounds provided in the CPC.
explanation: The cited Pakistan Code formulation lists four grounds; amendments in a particular jurisdiction require separate checking.
cue: The cited Pakistan Code formulation lists four grounds; amendments in a particular jurisdiction require separate checking.

subject: CPC
question: As per Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, Order VII Rule 11, the plaint shall be rejected in all following cases BUT:
options: Where it does not disclose a cause of action
Where the suit appears from the statement in the plaint to be barred by any law
Where the relief claimed is under-valued and the plaintiff, on being required by the Court to correct the valuation within a time to be fixed by the Court, fails to do so
Where the plaintiff seeks the recovery of money, the plaint stated the precise amount claimed
explanation: Stating the precise money claim complies with rule 2; it is not a rejection ground. The printed key A is wrong.
cue: Stating the precise money claim complies with rule 2; it is not a rejection ground

subject: CPC
question: As per Order VII Rule 12 of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908, where a plaint is rejected, the Judge shall record order to that effect with the reasons for such _____.
explanation: Order VII rule 12 requires the Judge to record an order rejecting the plaint, with reasons for such order. The printed answer B matches the cited Pakistan Code wording.
cue: Rejection: record an order with reasons.

subject: CPC
question: As per Order VII Rule 22(1) of the CPC 1908, where a party is not found at the address given by him for service and no agent or _____ member of his family on whom a notice, summons or other process can be served is present, a copy of the notice, summons or other process shall be fixed to the outer door of the house.
explanation: The cited rule uses adult male member; this is the wording of the source provision, not a general rule for every service situation.
cue: The cited rule uses adult male member; this is the wording of the source provision, not a general rule for every service situation.

subject: CPC
question: As per Order VIII, Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908, the defendant shall at or before the first hearing or within such time as the Court may permit, present _____ his defence.
explanation: The defendant's pleading is a written statement of defence. Time limits may vary with amendments.
cue: The defendant's pleading is a written statement of defence

subject: CPC
question: As per Order VIII Rule 3 of the CPC 1908, it shall not be sufficient for a defendant in his written statement to deny generally the ground alleged by the plaintiff, but the defendant must deal _____ with each allegation of fact of which he does not admit the truth, except damages.
explanation: Specific denials are required; a general denial is insufficient.
cue: Specific denials are required; a general denial is insufficient.

subject: CPC
question: As per Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 Order VIII Rule 4, where a defendant denies an allegation of fact in the _____, he must not do so evasively but answer the point of substance.
explanation: The denial must meet the substance of the allegation in the plaint.
cue: The denial must meet the substance of the allegation in the plaint.

subject: CPC
question: As per illustration (c) of Order VIII, Rule 6 of The Code of Civil Procedure 1908, A sues B on a bill of exchange. B alleges that A has wrongfully neglected to ensure B's goods and is liable to him in compensation which he claims to set-off. The amount not being ascertained _____.
explanation: A legal set-off under this rule requires an ascertained sum; unassessed damages do not qualify.
cue: A legal set-off under this rule requires an ascertained sum; unassessed damages do not qualify.

subject: CPC
question: As per Order VIII Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908, where any party from whom a written statement is so required fails to present the same within the time fixed by Court, the Court may pronounce judgment _____ or make such order in relation to the suit as it thinks fit.
explanation: The court may pronounce judgment against the defaulting party or make another appropriate order.
cue: The court may pronounce judgment against the defaulting party or make another appropriate order.

subject: CPC
question: As per Order IX Rule 3 of The Code of Civil Procedure 1908, where neither party appears when the suit is called on for hearing, the Court may make an order that the _____.
explanation: When neither side appears, dismissal is permitted.
cue: When neither side appears, dismissal is permitted.

subject: CPC
question: As per Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 Order IX, Rule 6, where the plaintiff appears and defendant does not appear when the suit is called on for hearing and it is proved that the summons was duly served, then the Court _____.
explanation: Due service plus the defendant's absence permits ex parte proceedings.
cue: Due service plus the defendant's absence permits ex parte proceedings.

subject: CPC
question: As per Order IX Rule 6(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908, where it is owing to the plaintiff's default that the summons was not _____ or was not served insufficient time, the Court shall order the plaintiff to pay the costs occasioned by the postponement.
explanation: Plaintiff-caused failure of due or timely service attracts postponement costs. The source's insufficient time is a typographical error for in sufficient time.
cue: Plaintiff-caused failure of due or timely service attracts postponement costs

subject: CPC
question: Order _____ rule 13 of the CPC provides remedy against ex-parte decree.
explanation: Order IX rule 13 provides the application to set aside an ex parte decree.
cue: Order IX rule 13 provides the application to set aside an ex parte decree.

subject: CPC
question: As per Order IX rule 13(1) of the C.P.C, in any case, in which a decree is passed ex-parte against a defendant, he may apply to the Court by which the decree was passed for an order _____.
options: To give a notice to the other party
explanation: The relief is setting aside the decree, on the rule's stated grounds.
cue: The relief is setting aside the decree, on the rule's stated grounds.

subject: CPC
question: As per Order XXXIX Rule 3 of the CPC 1908, the court shall in all cases, before granting an injunction direct notice of the application for the same to be given to the _____.
explanation: Notice normally goes to the opposite party. The stem omits the exception where delay would defeat the object of the injunction.
cue: Notice normally goes to the opposite party

subject: CPC
question: As per Order XXXIX Rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908, any order for _____ may be discharged, or varied, or set aside by the Court on application made thereto by any party dissatisfied with such order.
explanation: Rule 4 concerns discharge, variation or setting aside of an injunction.

options: Unduly rigid and does not make room for any special law & procedure
Not unduly rigid and makes room for any special law & procedure and generally gives precedence to such special law and procedure (Reference: Section 1)
Not unduly rigid and makes room for any special law & procedure but generally gives precedence to the law & procedure given under the Code
explanation: Special law, special jurisdiction and prescribed special procedure are saved unless the Code specifically provides otherwise.
cue: Special law, special jurisdiction and prescribed special procedure are saved unless the Code specifically provides otherwise.

subject: CrPC
question: This Act may be called the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, and it shall come into force on the first day of _____ 1898.
explanation: The commencement date is 1 July 1898.
cue: The commencement date is 1 July 1898.

subject: CrPC
question: What is true to Code of Criminal Procedure _____.
options: It is mainly, though not purely, an adjective or procedural law
There are also certain provisions which are partly in the nature of substantive law
explanation: The book describes the Code as primarily procedural with some substantive elements. Its secondary citation has not been independently verified.

subject: CrPC
question: Cognizable offence under PPC has been defined _____.
explanation: Cognizable offences permit warrantless arrest in accordance with the Second Schedule or applicable law.
cue: Cognizable offences permit warrantless arrest in accordance with the Second Schedule or applicable law.

subject: CrPC
question: As per Section 4(j) of the Code of Criminal Procedure 1898, "High Court" means the highest court of _____ or revision for a province.
explanation: The definition refers to criminal appeal or revision.
cue: The definition refers to criminal appeal or revision.

subject: CrPC
question: As per The Code of Criminal Procedure 1898, Section 4(1) "Investigation" includes all the proceedings under this Code for the collection of evidence conducted by a police-officer or by any person (other than a Magistrate) who is authorized by a _____ in this behalf:
explanation: The authorized non-police investigator acts under a Magistrate's authorization.
cue: The authorized non-police investigator acts under a Magistrate's authorization.

subject: CrPC
question: As per section 4(1)(h) of the Cr.P.C, _____ means the allegation made orally or in writing to a Magistrate, with a view to his taking action, under this Code that some person whether known or unknown, has committed an offence, but it does not include the report of a police officer.
explanation: A complaint to a Magistrate is distinct from a police report and an FIR.
cue: A complaint to a Magistrate is distinct from a police report and an FIR.

subject: CrPC
question: As per section 4(1)(l) under the CrPC, _____ includes all the proceedings under this code for collection of evidence conducted by a Police Officer or any person (other than a Magistrate) who is authorized by a Magistrate on this behalf.
explanation: Collection of evidence by the stated investigator is investigation.
cue: Collection of evidence by the stated investigator is investigation.

subject: CrPC
question: If a private person arrests a person having reason to believe that person arrested is a proclaimed offender than the private person shall without any unnecessary delay shall make over arrested person to _____.
explanation: Hand the arrested person to a police officer, or take him to the nearest police station if none is available.
cue: Hand the arrested person to a police officer, or take him to the nearest police station if none is available.

subject: CrPC
question: As per Section 4(1)(k) of Criminal Procedure Code 1898, _____ includes every inquiry other than a trial conducted under this Code by a Magistrate or Court.
explanation: Inquiry is the judicial process other than trial; investigation collects evidence.
cue: Inquiry is the judicial process other than trial; investigation collects evidence.

subject: CrPC
question: In Cr.P.C "Offence" means any act or omission made punishable by any law for the time being in force; it also includes any act in respect of which a complainant may be made under Section 20 of the _____.
explanation: The definition expressly includes complaints under section 20 of the Cattle Trespass Act 1871.
cue: The definition expressly includes complaints under section 20 of the Cattle Trespass Act 1871.

subject: CrPC
question: The investigation report compiled by the officer in charge of the police station shall be forwarded to magistrate through _____.
explanation: The cited Code provides the report route through the Public Prosecutor.
cue: The cited Code provides the report route through the Public Prosecutor.

subject: CrPC
question: As per Section 46(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code 1898, in making an arrest the police officer or other person making the same shall actually _____ or confine the body of the person to be arrested, unless there, be a submission to the custody by word or action.
explanation: Arrest involves touching or confining the body unless the person submits to custody.
cue: Arrest involves touching or confining the body unless the person submits to custody.

subject: CrPC
question: Warrant is a _____.
explanation: A judicial warrant records an official act and is a public document.
cue: A judicial warrant records an official act and is a public document.

subject: CrPC
question: A warrant of arrest is a command _____.
options: Signed, sealed and issued by Magistrate

cue: The book intends D, but the wording is overbroad: warrants are issued by a Court, and may in specified circumstances be directed to persons other than police

subject: CrPC
question: As per section 50 of the Code of Criminal Procedure 1898, the person arrested _____ be subjected to more restraint than is necessary to prevent his escape.
explanation: Only restraint necessary to prevent escape is allowed.
cue: Only restraint necessary to prevent escape is allowed.

subject: CrPC
question: Under Section 58 of the Cr.P.C, a police-officer may, for the purpose of arresting without warrant, any person whom he is authorized to arrest under Chapter V, pursue such person into _____.
options: Within the jurisdiction of concerned police station only
Within the jurisdiction of concerned district only
Within the jurisdiction of concerned subdivision only
explanation: Authorized pursuit is not restricted to the officer's police-station or district boundary.
cue: Authorized pursuit is not restricted to the officer's police-station or district boundary.

subject: CrPC
question: As per section, 59 of the CrPC, a private person may arrest a person under the Cr.P.C who in his view commits _____.
options: A Non-bailable and cognizable offence or any proclaimed offender
explanation: The witnessed offence must be both non-bailable and cognizable; proclaimed offenders are a separate statutory category.
cue: The witnessed offence must be both non-bailable and cognizable; proclaimed offenders are a separate statutory category.

subject: CrPC
question: Under section _____ of Cr.P.C, a police officer making an arrest without warrant shall take or send the person arrested before Magistrate or before an officer in-charge of police station.
explanation: Section 60 requires production without unnecessary delay, subject to bail provisions.
cue: Section 60 requires production without unnecessary delay, subject to bail provisions.

subject: CrPC
question: As per The Code of Criminal Procedure 1898 section 61. Persons arrested not to be detained for more than twenty-four hours. No police-officer shall detain in custody a person arrested without warrant for a longer period than under all the circumstances of the case is reasonable.
explanation: Without a Magistrate's special order under section 167, the limit is 24 hours excluding necessary travel to court.
cue: Without a Magistrate's special order under section 167, the limit is 24 hours excluding necessary travel to court.

subject: CrPC
question: Which section of Cr. P.C. contemplates service of summons?
explanation: Section 69 addresses service of summons.
cue: Section 69 addresses service of summons.

subject: CrPC
question: _____ required under section 94 of Cr.P.C mere to produce a document or other thing shall be deemed to have compelled with the requisition if he causes such document or thing to be produced instead of attending personally to produce the same.
explanation: Any person required merely to produce an item can arrange its production rather than attend personally.
cue: Any person required merely to produce an item can arrange its production rather than attend personally.

subject: CrPC
question: As per Section 94(2) of the Cr. P. C, any person required under this section merely to produce a document or other thing _____ deemed to have complied with the requisition if he causes such document or thing to be produced instead of attending personally to produce the same.
explanation: Causing production fulfils a requisition solely for production.
cue: Causing production fulfils a requisition solely for production.

subject: CrPC
question: To which court _____ shall a person, who has interest in a book in respect of which in order of forfeiture has been made under section 99-A of the Cr.P.C, apply to set aside such an order.
explanation: The application to set aside the forfeiture order lies to the High Court under this provision.
cue: The application to set aside the forfeiture order lies to the High Court under this provision.

subject: CrPC
question: As per Section 99-B of Cr.P.C, "any person having any interest in any newspaper, book or other document in respect of which an order of forfeiture has been made under section 99A of Cr.P.C, or any other law from the date of such order, apply to _____ to set aside such order".
explanation: The High Court is the forum. The book omits words concerning the time limit from the quoted stem.
cue: The High Court is the forum

subject: CrPC
question: As per section 104 of the Code of Criminal Procedure 1898, _____ may, if it thinks fit, impound any document or thing produced before it under this code.
explanation: The power is conferred on any Court, not just one named class.
cue: The power is conferred on any Court, not just one named class.

subject: CrPC
question: When any Magistrate not empowered to proceed under section 107(1) of the Cr.P.C has reason to believe that any person is likely to commit a breach of the peace which cannot be prevented otherwise than by detaining such person in custody, such Magistrate may _____ for his arrest.
options: After recording his reasons, order his arrest
After recording his reasons, issue a warrant
explanation: The provision requires recorded reasons and a warrant, subject to the statutory process.
cue: The provision requires recorded reasons and a warrant, subject to the statutory process.

subject: CrPC
question: Under which section _____ of Cr.P.C can a Magistrate of 1st class require habitual robber, house-breaker, thief or forger within his jurisdiction to execute a bound which sureties for his good behavior for a period of 3 years.
explanation: Section 110 concerns security for good behaviour from habitual offenders for a period not exceeding three years.
cue: Section 110 concerns security for good behaviour from habitual offenders for a period not exceeding three years.

subject: CrPC
question: As per Section 113 of the Criminal Procedure Code 1898, if the person in respect of whom order under Section 112 of the Cr.P.C is made is present in Court, it shall be _____ to him or, if he so desires, the substance thereof shall be explained to him.
explanation: Read the order over, or explain its substance if requested.
cue: Read the order over, or explain its substance if requested.

subject: CrPC
question: As per section 116 of the Code of Criminal Procedure 1898, the Magistrate may, if he sees sufficient cause, dispense with the personal attendance of any person called upon to show-cause why he should not be ordered to execute a bond for keeping the peace, and may permit him to appear by _____.
explanation: The permitted substitute appearance is by a pleader.
cue: The permitted substitute appearance is by a pleader.

subject: CrPC
question: As per Section 135 (B) The Code of Criminal Procedure Code 1898, the person against whom such order is made shall appear in accordance with such order and either show cause against the same, or apply to the Magistrate by whom it was made to appoint a jury to try whether the same is _____.
explanation: The quoted provision asks whether the nuisance-removal order is reasonable and proper.
cue: The quoted provision asks whether the nuisance-removal order is reasonable and proper.

subject: CrPC
question: As per Section 137(1) of Criminal Procedure Code 1898, if he (a person against whom an order has been passed under section 133 of the Cr.P.C) appears and shows cause against the order, the Magistrate shall take _____.
explanation: The Magistrate takes evidence in the manner provided in Chapter XX, as the cited text of section 137(1) specifies.
cue: The Magistrate takes evidence in the matter as in a summons case.

subject: CrPC
question: As per Section 143 of the Cr.P.C, a magistrate of the 1st class may order any person not to repeat or continue a public nuisance, as defined in the _____ or any special or local law.
explanation: The definition reference is the Pakistan Penal Code. The printed key B wrongly points back to CrPC.
cue: The definition reference is the Pakistan Penal Code

subject: CrPC
question: As per section 144(3) of the Cr.P.C, an order under this section may be directed to a particular individual or to the _____ when frequenting visiting a particular place.
explanation: An order may address the public generally when frequenting or visiting a particular place.
cue: An order may address the public generally when frequenting or visiting a particular place.

subject: CrPC
question: Section _____ of Cr.P.C deals with information of cognizable offences.
explanation: Information relating to commission of a cognizable offence is recorded under section 154.
cue: Information relating to commission of a cognizable offence is recorded under section 154.

subject: CrPC
question: As per section 155(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure 1898, when information is given to an officer in charge of a police station of the commission within the limits of such station of a non-cognizable offense, he shall enter a book to be kept as aforesaid the substance of such information and refer the information to the _____.
explanation: The statute says refer the informant to the Magistrate; the book prints information instead of informant.
cue: The statute says refer the informant to the Magistrate; the book prints information instead of informant.

subject: CrPC
question: A Magistrate of the 1st Class or 2nd Class Magistrate specially empowered has the power to direct the police to investigate into non cognizable offence in PPC under _____.
explanation: Non-cognizable investigation requires the order specified in section 155(2).
cue: Non-cognizable investigation requires the order specified in section 155(2).

subject: CrPC
question: A Magistrate has the power under Cr. P.C. to direct the police to investigate into _____.
options: Only a non-cognizable offence, as in a cognizable offence the police is under a duty to investigate
explanation: Both categories are covered by distinct provisions; 156(3) alone concerns cognizable investigation.
cue: Both categories are covered by distinct provisions; 156(3) alone concerns cognizable investigation.

subject: CrPC
question: As per Section 158(1) of Criminal Procedure Code 1898, every report sent to a Magistrate under Section 157 shall, if the Provincial Government so directs, be submitted through such _____ as the Provincial Government, by general or special order, appoints in that behalf.
explanation: The specified channel is a superior officer of police appointed for that purpose.
cue: The specified channel is a superior officer of police appointed for that purpose.

subject: CrPC
question: The Magistrate shall make memorandum at the foot of record of confession to the effect at provided in section _____ of the criminal procedure code 1998.
explanation: Section 164 prescribes the confession memorandum. The book's year 1998 is a typo for 1898.
cue: Section 164 prescribes the confession memorandum

subject: CrPC
question: As per Section 164(1-A) of Criminal Procedure Code 1898, any such statement may be recorded by such Magistrate (Magistrate of first and second class) in the presence of the accused and the accused given an opportunity of _____ the witness making the statement.
explanation: The stated opportunity is cross-examination of the witness; recording authority remains subject to the section's qualifications.
cue: The stated opportunity is cross-examination of the witness; recording authority remains subject to the section's qualifications.

subject: CrPC
question: As per The Code of Criminal Procedure 1898, Section 168 when any _____ has made any investigation under this chapter, he shall report the result of such investigation to the officer in charge of the police-station.
explanation: A subordinate officer reports investigation results to the station officer in charge.
cue: A subordinate officer reports investigation results to the station officer in charge.

subject: CrPC
question: As per section 200 of the Code of Criminal Procedure 1898, A magistrate taking cognizance of an offense on the complaint shall at once examine the complainant upon oath, and the substance of the examination shall be reduced to writing and shall be signed by the complainant, and also by the _____.
explanation: The Magistrate also signs the written substance of the examination, subject to the section's exceptions.
cue: The Magistrate also signs the written substance of the examination, subject to the section's exceptions.

subject: CrPC
question: As per The Code of Criminal Procedure 1898, Section 201. Procedure by Magistrate not competent to take cognizance of the case. (1) If the complaint has been made in writing to a Magistrate who is not competent to take cognizance of the case, he shall return the complaint for presentation to the _____ to that effect.
explanation: Return the written complaint for presentation to the proper court with an endorsement.
cue: Return the written complaint for presentation to the proper court with an endorsement.

subject: CrPC
question: As per Section 201(1) of Criminal Procedure Code 1898, if the complaint has been made in writing to a _____ who is not competent to take cognizance of the case; he shall return the complaint for presentation to the proper Court with an endorsement to that effect.
explanation: This procedure addresses a Magistrate lacking competence to take cognizance.
cue: This procedure addresses a Magistrate lacking competence to take cognizance.

subject: CrPC
question: As per section 202(2) of the Cr.P.C, a court of session may, instead of directing an investigation under the provision of sub-section (1), direct the investigation to be made by any magistrate subordinate to it for the purpose of ascertaining the _____ of the complaint.
explanation: The inquiry or investigation assesses the truth or falsehood of the complaint before process issues.
cue: The inquiry or investigation assesses the truth or falsehood of the complaint before process issues.

subject: CrPC
question: As per section 204(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure 1898, when by any law for the time being in force any process fees or other fees are payable, no process shall be issued until the fees are paid, and if such fees are not paid within a _____ Time the court may dismiss the complaint.
explanation: Failure to pay within a reasonable time permits dismissal.
cue: Failure to pay within a reasonable time permits dismissal.

subject: CrPC
question: The session court is competent to acquit an accused during trial at any stage under _____ Cr.P.C.
explanation: Section 265K permits acquittal where there is no probability of conviction after hearing the prosecutor and accused and recording reasons. The printed key B is wrong.
cue: Section 265K permits acquittal where there is no probability of conviction after hearing the prosecutor and accused and recording reasons

subject: CrPC
question: Predecessor is _____.
options: One who goes after another in a given state, position or office, and does not necessarily expresses any relation of illegal privity
One who goes before another in a given state, position or office, and does not necessarily expresses any relation of legal privity (Reference: Section 350)
One who goes before another in a given state, position or office, and does not necessarily expresses any relation of illegal privity
One who goes after another in a given state, position or office, and does not necessarily expresses any relation of legal privity
explanation: Predecessor means the earlier holder of the office; successor means the later one. The extended wording is the book's explanation, not a statutory definition.
cue: Predecessor means the earlier holder of the office; successor means the later one

subject: CrPC
question: As per section 404 of the Cr.P.C, "_____ shall lie from any judgment or order of a Criminal Court except as provided for by this Code or by any other law for the time being in force".
explanation: A criminal appeal must be authorized by law; it is not automatic from every order.
cue: A criminal appeal must be authorized by law; it is not automatic from every order.

subject: CrPC
question: As per section 406-A of the Cr.P.C, "Any person aggrieved by an order refusing to accept or reject a surety under section 122 may appeal against such order to the _____".
explanation: The appeal lies to the Court of Session under the cited provision.
cue: The appeal lies to the Court of Session under the cited provision.

subject: CrPC
question: As per Section 408 of the Criminal Procedure Code 1898, any person convicted on a trial held by an Assistant Sessions Judge, a District Magistrate (Special Magistrate) or a Judicial Magistrate, or any person sentenced under Section 349 of the Cr.P.C may appeal to the _____.
explanation: Court of Session is the general forum under this section; the book omits exceptions in its provisos.
cue: Court of Session is the general forum under this section; the book omits exceptions in its provisos.

subject: CrPC
question: As per section 410 of the Cr.P.C, "Any person convicted on a trial held by a Sessions Judge, or an additional Sessions Judge, may appeal to _____".
explanation: An appeal from a Sessions or Additional Sessions Judge conviction goes to the High Court.
cue: An appeal from a Sessions or Additional Sessions Judge conviction goes to the High Court.

subject: CrPC
question: As per section 412 of the Cr.P.C, notwithstanding anything hereinbefore contained, where an accused person has pleaded guilty and has been convicted by a High Court, A court of session or Magistrate of First Class on such plea, there _____ appeal except as either extent or legality of the sentence.
explanation: The permitted challenge is to the extent or legality of sentence, not a general appeal against the guilty-plea conviction.
cue: The permitted challenge is to the extent or legality of sentence, not a general appeal against the guilty-plea conviction.

subject: CrPC
question: As per Section 419. Of The Code of Criminal Procedure 1898, Every appeal shall be made in the form of _____ in writing presented by the appellant or his pleader, and every such petition shall (unless the Court to which it is presented otherwise directs) be accompanied by a copy of the judgment or order appealed against.
explanation: Criminal appeals use a petition in writing; contrast the CPC memorandum of appeal.
cue: Criminal appeals use a petition in writing; contrast the CPC memorandum of appeal.

subject: CrPC
question: Give your legal opinion as per Section 429 of the Cr.P.C. when judges composing the Court of appeal are equally divided in opinion regarding a criminal case _____.
options: It shall be appealed to the Higher Court
The decision of the senior judge shall prevail
A fresh trial should be held
It shall be laid before another judge of the same court
explanation: The case and opinions go to another judge of the same court; the senior judge does not automatically prevail.
cue: The case and opinions go to another judge of the same court; the senior judge does not automatically prevail.

subject: CrPC
question: As per section 497(1) of the Cr.P.C, when any person accused of any non-bailable offence is arrested or detained without warrant by an officer in charge of a police station, or appears or is brought before a Court, he _____ released on-bail.
explanation: May is the opening rule, subject to the prohibitory clause and statutory exceptions. Non-bailable does not mean bail is impossible.
cue: May is the opening rule, subject to the prohibitory clause and statutory exceptions

subject: CrPC
question: Which of the following deals with the discharge from custody?
explanation: Section 500 addresses discharge once the required bond is executed, subject to other lawful detention.
cue: Section 500 addresses discharge once the required bond is executed, subject to other lawful detention.

subject: CrPC
question: As per section 502(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure 1898, all or any sureties for the attendance and appearance of a person released on bail may _____ apply to a magistrate to discharge the bond, either wholly or so far as relates to the applicants.
explanation: Sureties can apply at any time; the section then prescribes the procedure.
cue: Sureties can apply at any time; the section then prescribes the procedure.

subject: CrPC
question: The early release of prisoner is called _____.

cue: The likely intended concept is parole, but early release can also result from remission or other mechanisms

subject: CrPC
question: Salman is continuously detained for a non-bailable offence not punishable with death for 25 months. Give your legal opinion as per the Cr.P.C, whether Salman can be granted bail:
options: No, if the trial is delayed by his own omission
No, if the trial is delayed by the prosecution
Yes, if the trial is not delayed by his action or omission
No, because it's the discretion of the court

subject: CrPC
question: Which classification of offence comes under Criminal Procedure Code?
explanation: The book keys all of these. However the cited Pakistan Code has omitted the former summons-case and warrant-case definitions at section 4(1)(v) and (w). Both A and C remain valid classifications, with no combined option. Excluded from scored mocks.
cue: Check current classifications, not an old all-of-these key.

subject: CrPC
question: Classification of offences given in the Code of Criminal Procedure under _____.
explanation: The Second Schedule tabulates offences and procedural classifications.
cue: The Second Schedule tabulates offences and procedural classifications.

subject: CrPC
question: Classification of compoundable and non compoundable offences has been provided under _____.
explanation: The Second Schedule includes compoundability; section 345 supplies the governing compounding provisions and tables.
cue: The Second Schedule includes compoundability; section 345 supplies the governing compounding provisions and tables.

subject: CrPC
question: In which of the following accomplice is not competent witness _____.
options: Offences punishable with confiscation of property
explanation: Article 16 excludes offences punishable with hadd from its rule on accomplice competence.
cue: Article 16 excludes offences punishable with hadd from its rule on accomplice competence.

subject: CrPC
question: Trial is a judicial proceeding which ends in _____.
explanation: A completed trial ordinarily determines conviction or acquittal; this teaching shorthand does not cover every procedural termination.
cue: A completed trial ordinarily determines conviction or acquittal; this teaching shorthand does not cover every procedural termination.

subject: CrPC
question: If withdrawal of prosecution is made after charge has been framed, the accused shall get _____.
explanation: With court consent, withdrawal after charge results in acquittal; before charge the result is generally discharge.
cue: With court consent, withdrawal after charge results in acquittal; before charge the result is generally discharge.

subject: CrPC
question: Session judge can pass _____.
options: Any sentence authorized by law and death sentence subject to confirmation by High Courts
explanation: A Sessions or Additional Sessions Judge can impose any sentence authorized by law; death requires High Court confirmation.
cue: A Sessions or Additional Sessions Judge can impose any sentence authorized by law; death requires High Court confirmation.
